args.title: formatExportFilename() builds the date suffix with at.toISOString().slic
args.body:
File: src/exportUtils.ts

formatExportFilename() builds the date suffix with at.toISOString().slice(0,10), which is always UTC; it should format the date in the user's/report's local time zone (e.g. using Intl.DateTimeFormat with a tz parameter, similar to formatDay/localHour in util/dates.ts) so evening exports in zones behind UTC don't get tomorrow's date.

args.title: Update slugify so it preserves letters from non-Latin scripts (Greek, Cy
args.body:
File: src/util/strings.ts

Update slugify so it preserves letters from non-Latin scripts (Greek, Cyrillic, etc.) instead of stripping everything outside [a-z0-9] after NFKD normalization/lowercasing; e.g. use a Unicode-aware letter/number match (\p{L}\p{N}) rather than ASCII-only a-z0-9, so formatExportFilename in exportUtils.ts keeps the original report name's letters in export file names.

result: {"pull_request": "pr-138", "branch": "repomind/issue-4431", "state": "open"}

args.body:
label: feature
file: src/util/strings.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.
src/util/strings.ts's slugify() does value.normalize("NFKD").replace(accents).toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-"): this NFKD+accent-strip approach only recovers ASCII base letters from accented Latin characters, but Greek/Cyrillic characters have no ASCII decomposition, so they get matched by [^a-z0-9] and replaced with '-', producing empty/plain 'report-<date>' names as described in the issue. exportUtils.ts's formatExportFilename calls slugify(reportName) to build the export file name.
